title: Godfrey Hirsch, the Tulaneans, and why white bands were dance bands
summary: Weinstein describes dance-band custom in New Orleans: sets, stock arrangements, then faking two-beat tunes. There were no separate jazz bands.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Yes. Yes. Wade was in the Eastern Band too. So was Godfrey Hirsch. You see, as you're unconscious of these things come back to you. But Godfrey was a perennial student. Godfrey stayed at Warren Easton for six years, you know. I think he liked the atmosphere. And then he went to Tulane for about another 27. Yeah. And he played in the Tulaneans. Tell us about the Tulaneans. I don't know what you bought him. I didn't, I didn't work with that band. Godfrey played with that band. That was another, just a name to me. Were they a good jazz band? I would say it was fairly well liked. You know, there were no jazz bands per se with the white guys I played with. These were dance bands, right? So you'd go out with an eight-piece band or a nine-piece band. And with typical, the typical New Orleans custom, you played a few tunes. You played sets. You played from the old orchestrations, you know, the stocks. And you'd play three or four tunes. And then you'd play the waltz. And then as soon as the liquor started to work, then I didn't want to hear this anymore. Then you'd start to fake. You'd play all the standard fake tunes for the rest of the night. And I don't care whether you're talking about one of the dance halls or you're talking about at the country club. The custom followed exactly. As the evening progressed, you got into nothing but the traditional New Orleans two-beat tunes. And that's the way it was. But per se, no jazz bands. No jazz bands. No jazz bands. Every band played jazz. But you didn't have the typical combination, maybe, of, uh, we like to think about it, a piano, a banjo, and a trumpet,
a trombone, clarinet. No. What about Schofi and Leon Prima? What kind of band was that?
